evidence.intent_output: 502 with onError receiving exactly one ProxyException of kind INVALID_RESPONSE; the chunked body is never decoded or relayed

title: HTTP/1.0 backend response with Transfer-Encoding: chunked is decoded as chunked instead of rejected as faulty framing
description: RFC 9112 §6.1: 'A server or client that receives an HTTP/1.0 message containing a Transfer-Encoding header field MUST treat the message as if the framing is faulty, even if a Content-Length is present'; §6.3 then requires a proxy receiving a response with faulty framing to close the server connection, discard the response and send 502. SEC-PROXY-004 is explicitly 'stricter than the RFC' and lists smuggling as its threat, yet ResponseParser.status() throws away the HTTP minor version and framing() decodes 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK / Transfer-Encoding: chunked' as chunked and relays 200 'hello'. A backend (or anything between proxy and backend) that frames differently from the HTTP/1.0 semantics is accepted here, which is the exact desync class the requirement exists to close; this is the only place the parser is laxer than the RFC.
suggested_fix: Keep the minor version digit in ResponseParser.Head (e.g. boolean http10 from line.charAt(7)=='0'); in framing(), after the bodyless check, throw invalid("Transfer-Encoding on an HTTP/1.0 response") when head is HTTP/1.0 and transferEncodings is non-empty. HEAD/204/304 stay bodyless first (FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 unaffected). Reuse the probe above as the regression test in BackendResponseParserTest.
req: SEC-PROXY-004 (requirement statement: RFC 9112 §6.3 framing, stricter than the RFC; RFC 9112 §6.1)
